# Golden item sparkle

Build/rebuild with **Horror Game > Items > Build Golden Sparkle Prefabs**.

Shortcut: right-click a GameObject in the **Hierarchy** (including Prefab Mode), or a `.prefab` asset in the **Project** window, then choose **Horror Game > Add Golden Sparkle**. The tool adds the linked effect above the object's renderer bounds. Move the child to refine its position and edit its overrides in the Inspector. Existing sparkles are detected, so repeating the command does not add duplicates. Multiple selected objects/prefabs are supported. Hierarchy changes support Undo; the Project command saves the selected prefab assets directly. Imported model files such as FBX are not editable prefabs: use a regular prefab or a scene instance instead.

The shortcut also adds **Sparkle_TriggerArea** beneath the effect, with the target already assigned and a **2 second Entry Delay**. Its default box covers **1 x 1 x 1 metre**, centred on the effect. Select that child and use **BoxCollider > Edit Collider** to fit the room; change **Entry Delay** to tune the timer. Leaving before the delay cancels it. Existing sparkle-only objects can use the same menu again to add the missing trigger without duplicating the effect. Objects that already have a linked local trigger are skipped. An effect already configured for distance-only visibility keeps that setting; enable **Require Room Entry** to use its trigger.

For several items in one room, you can instead use one shared `Room_SparkleTrigger` and assign all effects to its **Targets** list. Disable the individual trigger areas in that case, so multiple triggers do not compete over visibility.

1. Parent `Item_GoldenSparkle.prefab` to a pickup. Position its origin just above the visible surface so the object does not hide it. It is a small gold glint, with no scene light or through-wall rendering. Pickup deactivation also hides its child effect.
2. Place `Room_SparkleTrigger.prefab` in the room. Resize its BoxCollider to cover the room interior (not the corridor). Keep it on the Default layer, which must collide with the player in the physics layer matrix.
3. Drag that room's sparkle components into the trigger's **Targets** list. After **Entry Delay** (default 2 seconds) inside, the glints start. Leaving early cancels the delay. By default leaving hides them and re-entry starts a fresh delay. **Keep Visible After Leaving** unlocks them for the current play session instead; this is not persisted in saves.
4. Tune **Tint** (alpha controls faintness), **Size**, **Pulse Duration**, **Pulse Interval**, **Fade Start Distance**, and **Maximum Distance** on each effect. Distance is measured from the registered player, which works with stationary cameras. Disable **Require Room Entry** for a distance-only hint. **Viewer** is an optional override for previews or other actors.

The effect reuses the template's SparkleFX particle renderer/material. No vendor assets or existing scenes/pickups are modified. To keep hints fair, avoid putting the trigger across a doorway or placing the effect behind the pickup's own mesh. Room timing uses scaled gameplay time; paused gameplay does not advance it.

Visibility troubleshooting: in Play mode, select the **ItemGoldenSparkle** component (below Particle System) to see its live status: waiting for the room timer, out of range, no player, or active. **Preview Sparkle for 5 Seconds** temporarily bypasses trigger and distance without changing the saved settings. The native Particle System Play button cannot preview script-driven emission. **Minimum Screen Size** keeps the star readable at low render resolutions (default 0.08 of billboard screen height; the star's bright centre is only a small portion of its texture). Walls still occlude it. Default world size is 0.12 m and tint alpha 0.5. Existing explicit instance overrides remain in effect.

Use **Horror Game > Tests > Check Cigarette Sparkle** in Play mode for an existing cigarette pickup with a linked trigger. It temporarily positions the real player inside the area, checks the entry delay and particles, captures an isolated 320 x 180 render from 5 m, and restores player position/settings. Reports and captures go to ignored `Exports/Reviews/Sparkle`. Tests do not save the open scene. A trigger high on a shelf requires the player's capsule to reach it; a 1 m cube does not cover the entire room.
